Prevention: Clean tools and farm machinery to prevent tubers being spread
Consider direct controls for established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Do not accept potentially contaminated planting materials, e.g. soil on planting stock
Monitoring: Erect, perennial sedge (30-60 cm high), with extensive underground network tubers.
Tubers dark brown/black, irregular shaped, 1-2 cm long with several buds.
Leaves linear with distinct midrib, 7 mm wide.
Inflorescence with several unequal 'branches', each 2-6 cm long, emerging from the tip of the stem; each with 3-8 purplish- brown flowerheads
Inspect fields regularly (biweekly), in particular shortly after rainfall event, and consider direct control when found
Look out for it in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread tubers
Direct Control: Tubers and rhizomes in the soil can be destroyed by exposing to sunlight by ploughing.
This causes the tubers to dessicate (most effective in dry soil) and exhausts their food reserves
Place organic mulch over areas where weed is expected to grow - provides temporary suppression
Nursery soil solarization using white plastic sheet for two weeks that will generate heat to kill tubers of the weed
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Few herbicides kill the weed, but glyphosate has been found to be effective.
SC) is a post-emergence herbicide applied once the weed has germinated and before tobacco is sown.
Use at a rate of 23 ml in a 15 litre tank
